case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns collection of information required to prepare a Bluetooth qualification cost estimate for a product that combines a wireless module and a custom antenna. During review of the customer's questionnaire, the consultant identifies missing qualification-critical information that prevents accurate scoping. The discussion focuses on declaration fee handling and Host Stack qualification details. Follow-up clarification is requested because the customer's response regarding Host Stack usage is ambiguous and affects qualification planning.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The consultant explains that a Bluetooth qualification estimate cannot be prepared without understanding how the Bluetooth SIG Declaration Fee will be handled and without identifying the Host Stack qualification basis. The customer is asked to provide the Host Stack QDID or Design Number and implemented profiles because these are key inputs for determining qualification scope. When the customer responds that the Host Stack is 'not used,' the consultant recognizes that this statement is technically ambiguous. Clarification is requested to determine whether the product truly has no Host layer implementation or whether a Host implementation exists but lacks a qualified QDID/DN.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The qualification approach depends on the architecture and qualification status of the Host Stack. A valid estimate requires knowing whether an existing qualified Host design can be reused or whether an unqualified Host implementation must be addressed. Ambiguous statements such as 'none' or 'not used' cannot be accepted without determining whether the Host layer is absent or merely unqualified.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: An inaccurate qualification estimate may be produced if the Host Stack qualification status is misunderstood. Reuse opportunities could be missed, or required qualification work could be omitted from the project scope. This can lead to incorrect planning, qualification delays, and later rework when the actual Host architecture becomes known.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: During Bluetooth qualification scoping, always verify the Host Stack architecture and qualification pedigree explicitly. If a customer states that a Host Stack or profile is 'not used,' determine whether the function is genuinely absent or simply lacks an existing QDID/DN, because the distinction directly affects qualification scope, reuse strategy, and cost estimation.
